summary: Two-project integration brief: Tool Gate is a Rust library/CLI that evaluates caller-supplied tool metadata and invocation envelopes, producing deterministic allow, deny, or review-required receipts without executing tools (README.md:5-13). Agent Loop proposes autonomous work and tool invocations, while Tool Gate supplies the pre-execution policy decision (README.md:51-56). Their shared safety boundary is the transition from agent intent to runtime permission: no side effect should occur until Tool Gate returns allow, and review-required decisions must reach an operator (README.md:17-20,35-49). Actionable integration: make Agent Loop submit every proposed invocation to Tool Gate and require the execution runtime to verify and persist the resulting receipt before dispatch; deny or review on every non-allow result. Tool Gate risk: it trusts caller-supplied metadata and is not a sandbox, authentication layer, or execution runtime, so false risk, mutation, idempotency, or target declarations can yield unsafe decisions unless metadata is independently trusted (README.md:5-13,156-158; src/types.rs:22-40). Agent Loop risk: any direct runtime path that bypasses receipt enforcement turns proposals into ungoverned side effects; production systems are explicitly warned not to permit this bypass (README.md:31-33). Declared clean-tree check passed; inspection was read-only and created no artifacts.
